newsitem.title: USA: Digital shopping equipment unit -- source.
newsitem.headline: Digital shopping equipment unit -- source.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp. is looking to sell its computer network equipment business, whole or in parts, a source close to the company said Monday.
"The parts of it may be shopped around a little bit," the source said. "It's sort of been talked about for a year."
The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the situation, reported Monday that Digital has held talks about the unit's sale with Bain Capital Inc. and Lucent Technologies Inc.

Digital sees the networking unit, which has estimated annual revenues of about $600 million and could fetch $500 million to $750 million, as a growing cash drain that would take a huge investment to revive, the newspaper said.
Digital said in a statement Monday that its networking business includes areas that are integral to its strategy.

"In order to best meet customer and channel partner needs, we always are looking at a variety of possible relationships with other companies to optimize our network solutions for our customers," it said.
"We will announce these relationships when they occur, if appropriate. Until that time, we cannot comment on rumour or speculation."
Digital stock rose $1.06 cents to $44.81 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
